Karthik / Marissa / Dylan —

I pulled the SFDC export against the MW CSV and found a few discrepancies we should resolve before final ROI numbers:

Summary of findings:
- 28 total leads in MW export matched to contacts in SFDC.
- 7 became opportunities within 14 days; total ACV $164,000.
- Of those 7, three opportunities are currently attributed to campaign "Q3ContentPush" in SFDC instead of "Midwest2026". Those three account for $102,000 of the $164k.
- 2 leads were deduped incorrectly during our last import (we need to check the fuzzy-match threshold).

Recommendation:
1) Reassign campaign on the three opps to the event campaign if the opportunity was first touched at the booth (we have timestamped activity logs).
2) Update import dedupe rules to use email > company name > title ordering for this file.
3) Run a 7-day appeal window with Alicia and SponsorOps to confirm disputed credits.

Attaching export: SFDC-opps-export.csv — will redact internal PII in a follow-up.

Thanks everyone for the call earlier. Per discussion, here are the agreed next steps and final attribution rules for the Midwest Roadshow ROI: 

Final decisions:
- Credit rule: Primary credit to event (Midwest2026) if the first demonstrated interest (booth form or demo QR) timestamp predates any prior digital engagement with Redwood. Partner credit applied when the prospect explicitly selected a sponsor-assisted demo or used a sponsor-distributed private link.
- The three disputed opps (SFDC IDs 005A, 005B, 005C) will be reassigned to campaign "Midwest2026". Laura will update SFDC by EOD Monday.
- Dedupe rule updated: email exact match first, then company fuzzy match (threshold 85), then title. Dylan to update import script and re-run on the MW export.
- HubSpot: we will create a static list "Midwest2026 - final" and push the normalized contacts. Karthik to own the push.

Attachments: midwest-retro-notes.pdf (final summary), Roadshow-scorecard.xlsx (updated), SFDC-opps-export.csv (redacted).
